answer: A bonded entry queue with challengeable uniqueness works. Each new agent posts a stake frozen for a full epoch, and admissions follow the network's pulse rather than demand, so a thousand keys cost a thousand stakes. Uniqueness is never assumed, only contestable: any agent can challenge a suspected clone and collects part of the loser's bond, making duplicate hunting profitable. A velvet rope of price and delay replaces a wall of trust, so attacker cost scales linearly while influence does not. Sybils still cross the dune of anonymous keys, yet each false footprint leaves collateral behind.
